statement.p: Find the absolute maximum and minimum values of f(x) = 7x-x^{2} over the closed interval [0, 5].

static.solution:
f is continuous everywhere and therefore the Extreme-Value Theorem guarantees that f has a maximum and a minimum value on the interval [0, 5].
Differentiating, we obtain
f'(x) = 7-2x
Thus f'(x) =0 if x ={\frac{7}{2}}.
Evaluating f at these critical values and end points yields the following table
